title: Drift Prevention
hook: Nothing's broken, so I haven't looked at it in months. That's exactly how things break.
statement: Without regular correction, every system declines. Drift grows the longer you go without checking.
explainer: No complaints doesn't mean no problems. Small slips pile up quietly, and the longer you wait to audit, the bigger and messier the fix gets.
sop: Rate your current Deviation from standard for one key system, 1 to 10.
Note the Time since your last real audit, in months.
If it's been more than a quarter, book the audit this week.
Pull the system back to standard and write down what slipped.
Set a recurring reminder so the next audit isn't left to memory.
equation_example: Deviation 5, Time 3 months since your last audit. 5 × 3 = 15 drift points. Higher means the gap between your standard and reality keeps growing. Lower means regular audits are keeping drift near zero.
question: Write the date of your last real system audit. Be honest.
closing_statement: No news isn't the same as no drift.
caption:
Principle Nº 160: Drift Prevention

Nothing's broken, so I haven't looked at it in months. That's exactly how things break.

Without regular correction, every system declines. Drift grows the longer you go without checking.

Your turn: Write the date of your last real system audit. Be honest.
